correctness.rationale: For all finite classes with positive nonlinear multipliers, direct differentiation gives nonnegative curvature and strict curvature whenever a nontrivial nonlinear class is weighted. Rolle, monotone derivative, and phase-line signs prove necessity/sufficiency for exactly two interior roots; an explicit two-class weight-ratio argument proves feasibility. The affine mixing-path implicit-function expansion yields the positive quadratic coefficient, with all denominators positive and endpoint inequalities controlled. Independently written rational checker passed 1,555 assertions, including explicit three-order coefficient; computations are checks, not proof.

value.rationale: The finite-mixture criterion solves a natural modeling uncertainty: exactly which distributions of social-group orders and signed nonlinear responses permit stable active coexistence alongside stable full cooperation. It excludes higher interior multiplicity even when many independent game types coexist, supplies an interpretable pair of linear inequalities for mixture design, and determines the otherwise invisible quadratic width of a near-critical phase window. An admissible rational three-order family realizes the coefficient, demonstrating more than a renamed two-order case.
